bugs.error_message: cli 'Failed to parse <contract>: ' with EMPTY exception message → looked like a silent failure; actually a read timeout
bugs.root_cause: httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=900.0) in parse_document was too tight for the 137-page contract: OCR takes ~14-16 min, and a cold OCR engine (fresh rebuild) pushed one run to 15.6 min → httpx.ReadTimeout. ReadTimeout's str() is EMPTY in this httpx version, so the cli's `logger.warning('Failed to parse %s: %s', key, exc)` printed a bare trailing colon, masquerading as a silent/empty error rather than a timeout.
bugs.fix: Bumped parse_document httpx timeout 900s → 1800s (30 min margin). Diagnosis lesson: an empty exception string from an httpx call is almost always a TimeoutException; don't read it as 'unknown failure' — check the elapsed wall-clock vs the configured timeout. (Long-term: a 137-page single-POST OCR is the wrong shape for 1000-doc batches — T6 should queue per-doc jobs, not block on one giant request.)
